display.purpose: Boot splash brand text only. Never used in the running UI.

headline.purpose: Window section headings. OS-register content identifiers.

title.purpose: Titlebar labels, taskbar items, clock. System chrome; the menus are set in Sans.

body.purpose: Human-facing content — about copy, contact items. Sans register.

label.purpose: Stack chips, captions, terminal lines, form labels. Smallest system text.

shadows.purpose: Default raised state for windows, buttons, taskbar, start menu.

shadows.name: bevel-in
shadows.value: border: 1px solid; border-top-color: #808080; border-left-color: #808080; border-right-color: #ffffff; border-bottom-color: #ffffff; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 #404040, inset -1px -1px 0 #dfdfdf
shadows.purpose: Pressed or sunken state for active buttons, inputs, content areas, status-bar panels, the tray well.

shadows.name: win-drop
shadows.purpose: Window frames and dialogs. Pixel-offset, zero blur — maintains the hardware aesthetic.

motion.name: win-boot
motion.purpose: Window entry — scales from 0.92 to 1. Decisive, no ease-in.

motion.name: taskbar-land
motion.purpose: Taskbar entry when window opens. Subtle overshoot.

motion.name: start-up
motion.purpose: Start menu fly-up. Fast, no drama.

motion.name: cursor-blink
motion.purpose: Terminal cursor. Hard step — no crossfade.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Stacked layout, no tilt, no absolute positioning.

breakpoints.name: desktop
breakpoints.purpose: OS shell mode: locked viewport, absolutely-positioned windows, internal window scrolling.

components.name: Win95 Button
components.description: Mechanical push-button with bevel-out chrome. Presses in on active with a 1px padding shift — no transition.
components.css: .ds-win-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 70px; padding: 4px 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; color: #1a1a2e; background: #c0c0c0; border: 1px solid; border-top-color: #ffffff; border-left-color: #ffffff; border-right-color: #404040; border-bottom-color: #404040; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 #dfdfdf, inset -1px -1px 0 #808080; cursor: pointer; } .ds-win-btn:hover { background: #dfdfdf; } .ds-win-btn:active { padding: 5px 11px 3px 13px; border-top-color: #404040; border-left-color: #404040; border-right-color: #ffffff; border-bottom-color: #ffffff; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 #808080, inset -1px -1px 0 #dfdfdf; } .ds-win-btn:focus-visible { outline: 1px dotted #000080; outline-offset: -3px; }

components.name: Win95 Input Field
components.description: Sunken input well. Bevel-in border signals receptacle. Dotted focus ring in titlebar navy.

components.name: Win95 Window
components.description: The signature component. Draggable frame with a FLAT navy titlebar (no gradient — the gradient was Win98), a 16px pixel-icon left of the label, caption buttons whose glyphs are inline SVG bitmaps, and the win drop shadow. Every window that is not on top drops to Inactive Gray.

about.txt - Notepad

I build software end-to-end — from the database schema up to the pixel on screen.
components.css: .ds-win95-window { background: #c0c0c0; border: 1px solid; border-top-color: #ffffff; border-left-color: #ffffff; border-right-color: #404040; border-bottom-color: #404040; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 #dfdfdf, inset -1px -1px 0 #808080, 4px 4px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.18); display: flex; flex-direction: column; width: 320px; } .ds-win95-titlebar { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 2px 2px 2px 6px; margin: 2px; background: #000080; color: #ffffff; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.8125rem; letter-spacing: 0.02em; user-select: none; cursor: default; } .ds-win95-window--inactive .ds-win95-titlebar { background: #808080; color: #c0c0c0; } .ds-win95-title-icon { width: 16px; height: 16px; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-win95-title-icon svg { display: block; image-rendering: pixelated; } .ds-win95-title { flex: 1; } .ds-win95-btns { display: flex; gap: 2px; } .ds-titlebar-btn { width: 16px; height: 14px; padding: 0; display: grid; place-items: center; color: #1a1a2e; background: #c0c0c0; border: 1px solid; border-top-color: #ffffff; border-left-color: #ffffff; border-right-color: #404040; border-bottom-color: #404040; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 #dfdfdf, inset -1px -1px 0 #808080; cursor: pointer; } .ds-titlebar-btn svg { display: block; } .ds-titlebar-btn:hover { background: #dfdfdf; } .ds-titlebar-btn--close { margin-left: 2px; } .ds-titlebar-btn--close:hover { background: #d44; } .ds-titlebar-btn:active { border-top-color: #404040; border-left-color: #404040; border-right-color: #ffffff; border-bottom-color: #ffffff; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 #808080, inset -1px -1px 0 #dfdfdf; } .ds-win95-content { margin: 0 2px 2px; padding: 1rem; background: #fdfdfd; border: 1px solid; border-top-color: #808080; border-left-color: #808080; border-right-color: #ffffff; border-bottom-color: #ffffff; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 #404040, inset -1px -1px 0 #dfdfdf; }

components.name: Explorer Tile
components.description: A project in the my work explorer. Selection paints the LABEL navy and leaves the 32px icon and the tile box alone; keyboard focus is a separate dotted marquee, because where the keyboard is and what the detail pane is showing are two different claims.
components.css: .ds-tile-grid { background: #fdfdfd; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(100px, 1fr)); align-content: start; gap: 2px; padding: 8px; } .ds-tile { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 6px 4px; background: transparent; border: 1px solid transparent; cursor: default; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; } .ds-tile-icon { display: block; flex: none; } .ds-tile-label { display: inline-block; max-width: 100px; padding: 0 2px; font-size: 0.65rem; line-height: 1.3; text-align: center; color: #1a1a2e; word-break: break-word; } .ds-tile[data-selected='true'] .ds-tile-label { background: #000080; color: #ffffff; } .ds-tile:focus-visible { outline: none; } .ds-tile:focus-visible .ds-tile-label { outline: 1px dotted #1a1a2e; outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-tile[data-selected='true']:focus-visible .ds-tile-label { outline-color: #ffffff; outline-offset: -1px; }

components.name: Game Counter
components.description: The LED readout in minesweeper.exe and snake.exe. SVG rectangles, not a seven-segment webfont: a third type family for six numerals would break the Mono/Sans split, and unlit segments are painted rather than omitted so a 1 still reads as a numeral in a slot.
components.css: .ds-counter { display: inline-flex; background: #000000; padding: 0; border: 1px solid; border-top-color: #404040; border-left-color: #404040; border-right-color: #ffffff; border-bottom-color: #ffffff; } .ds-counter svg { display: block; }

components.css: .ds-terminal { background: #0c0c0c; border: 1px solid #000000; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.6); padding: 14px 16px; } .ds-terminal-body { margin: 0; color: #33ff33; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.8125rem; line-height: 1.55; white-space: pre; } .ds-cursor { display: inline-block; width: 8px; height: 1em; background: #33ff33; vertical-align: -2px; animation: ds-cursor-blink 1s steps(1) infinite; margin-left: 2px; } @keyframes ds-cursor-blink { 0%, 50% { opacity: 1; } 50.01%, 100% { opacity: 0; } }

components.name: Display Properties Tabs
components.description: The property sheet's tab strip. The selected tab is 2px taller and covers the sheet's top edge, so the frame line breaks under it — that break is the whole reason a tab reads as the front of a stack. One tab stop for the strip; arrows move between pages.
components.html: Wallpaper
components.css: .ds-props { width: 260px; } .ds-props-tabs { display: flex; gap: 2px; padding-left: 3px; margin-bottom: -1px; position: relative; z-index: 1; } .ds-props-tab { margin-top: 2px; padding: 3px 11px 4px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; color: #1a1a2e; background: #c0c0c0; border: 1px solid; border-top-color: #ffffff; border-left-color: #ffffff; border-right-color: #404040; border-bottom-color: #c0c0c0; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 #dfdfdf, inset -1px 0 0 #808080; cursor: pointer; } .ds-props-tab:hover { background: #dfdfdf; } .ds-props-tab[aria-selected='true'] { margin-top: 0; padding-bottom: 6px; } .ds-props-sheet { padding: 12px; background: #c0c0c0; border: 1px solid; border-top-color: #ffffff; border-left-color: #ffffff; border-right-color: #404040; border-bottom-color: #404040; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 #dfdfdf, inset -1px -1px 0 #808080; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; color: #1a1a2e; }

components.name: Desktop Icon
components.description: OS desktop shortcut. 96px slot, transparent at rest. Hover, focus and active all highlight the LABEL — solid titlebar navy under white text with a 1px dotted white rectangle inset 1px — and leave the 32px glyph and the slot itself untouched, exactly as Win95 drew a selected shortcut. 88px below 1024px, where the icons become a wrapping row.
components.css: .ds-desktop-icon { width: 96px; padding: 4px; background: transparent; border: none; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 4px; cursor: pointer; color: #ffffff; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; text-align: center; } .ds-icon-label { display: inline-block; max-width: 100%; padding: 0 2px; background: transparent; white-space: normal; overflow-wrap: anywhere; line-height: 1.15; text-shadow: 1px 1px 0 #000000, 0 0 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.5); } .ds-desktop-icon:hover .ds-icon-label, .ds-desktop-icon:active .ds-icon-label, .ds-desktop-icon:focus-visible .ds-icon-label { background: #000080; color: #ffffff; outline: 1px dotted #ffffff; outline-offset: -1px; text-shadow: none; } .ds-desktop-icon:focus-visible { outline: none; } .ds-icon-glyph { width: 32px; height: 32px; display: block; } @media (max-width: 1023px) { .ds-desktop-icon { width: 88px; } }

components.name: Start Menu Item
components.description: A row in the Start menu or one of its fly-outs. Hover, keyboard focus and "this row's fly-out is open" are one visual state, because in Win95 they were one state. The label is Sans — Win95 set its menus in MS Sans Serif and kept the fixed-width face for terminals.
components.css: .ds-menu { min-width: 200px; margin: 0; padding: 4px 0; list-style: none; background: #c0c0c0; border: 1px solid; border-top-color: #ffffff; border-left-color: #ffffff; border-right-color: #404040; border-bottom-color: #404040; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 #dfdfdf, inset -1px -1px 0 #808080, 3px 3px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.15); } .ds-menu-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; width: 100%; padding: 0.3125rem 0.75rem; text-align: left; background: none; border: none; color: #1a1a2e; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; cursor: pointer; } .ds-menu-item:hover, .ds-menu-item:focus-visible, .ds-menu-item[aria-expanded='true'] { background: #000080; color: #ffffff; outline: none; } .ds-menu-item svg { width: 16px; height: 16px; flex-shrink: 0; image-rendering: pixelated; } .ds-menu-label { flex: 1; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-menu-arrow { flex-shrink: 0; padding-left: 1.25rem; font-size: 0.6875rem; line-height: 1; }

components.name: System Tray
components.description: One sunken well at the right end of the taskbar holding the speaker and the clock. No hover fill — a real tray icon never lit up; pressing shifts the glyph 1px down-right and leaves the well alone.
components.html: 14:32
components.css: .ds-tray { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 2px 6px; background: #c0c0c0; border: 1px solid; border-top-color: #808080; border-left-color: #808080; border-right-color: #ffffff; border-bottom-color: #ffffff; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 #404040, inset -1px -1px 0 #dfdfdf; } .ds-tray-btn { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 18px; height: 18px; padding: 0; background: none; border: none; color: #1a1a2e; cursor: pointer; } .ds-tray-btn svg { display: block; image-rendering: pixelated; } .ds-tray-btn:active svg { transform: translate(1px, 1px); } .ds-tray-btn:focus-visible { outline: 1px dotted #1a1a2e; outline-offset: 0; } .ds-tray-clock { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.8125rem; min-width: 42px; text-align: center; color: #1a1a2e; }

components.name: Boot Splash Flag
components.description: The flag on the boot splash: four panes inside a black outline that follows the wave, each pane's dark twin shading the columns the fold turns away from the light. A still of one frame — the shipped flag is three 48x28 character maps in src/lib/bootFlagFrames.js, painted at 5px per pixel and cycled on opacity alone, 350ms each. Frame 1 alone under prefers-reduced-motion.
components.css: .ds-flag { display: inline-block; filter: drop-shadow(4px 6px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.45)); } .ds-flag svg { display: block; image-rendering: pixelated; }

narrative.overview:
This is a 1990s operating system shell running on modern React, fully aware of what it is. The portfolio does not simulate Windows 95 as a novelty trick — it commits to the metaphor completely: draggable windows, a functioning taskbar, a boot sequence, a BSOD, Minesweeper, Snake. The visitor is not looking at a portfolio with a retro skin. They are using a machine.

The design system is built from the bevel. Every surface — buttons, windows, inputs, cards, the taskbar — uses the same four-layer double-border technique that Win95 used. Elevation is theatrical, not ambient: shadows exist because they are part of the performance. Typography follows a strict split: IBM Plex Mono for anything that belongs to the OS and IBM Plex Sans for anything that is human-facing content. One font family, two registers, complete discipline.
keyCharacteristics: Bevel-based elevation — four-layer double-border + inset shadow for every raised or sunken surface
Zero border radius — all OS chrome is pixel-sharp
Two-font discipline — Mono for the system, Sans for the person
Sky blue desktop gradient as the primary environment
Theatrical motion — animation is part of the OS illusion

rules.name: The One Focus Rule
rules.body: Active Window Blue (#000080) appears in exactly one place: the titlebar of the window on top — flat, no gradient. Every other titlebar drops to Inactive Gray, which is what makes focus readable at a glance. Its power comes from its exclusivity.

rules.name: The No-Pure-Extreme Rule
rules.body: No pure #000000 or #ffffff in any surface or text role. Every neutral is tinted.

rules.name: The System/Human Split Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono is the OS speaking. IBM Plex Sans is the person. Any new element that belongs to OS chrome uses Mono. Any element that is content uses Sans. The menus are the one exception, in Sans, because Win95 set its menus in MS Sans Serif.

rules.name: The Bevel-Only Rule
rules.body: All elevation is expressed through the bevel system. Do not add blurred box-shadow values to new OS-chrome components.

dos: Do use the bevel system for all new components with raised or pressed states.
Do use IBM Plex Mono for OS chrome and IBM Plex Sans for human-facing content.
Do keep all OS chrome at 0px border-radius.
Do use Active Window Blue exclusively on window titlebars and system focus rings.
Do include prefers-reduced-motion overrides for any new animation.
Do ask whether a new feature fits as a window, desktop icon, taskbar item, or dialog before inventing a new pattern.
Do animate with transform and opacity only, using ease-out-expo curves.
donts: Don't add border-radius to OS chrome components.
Don't add blurred box-shadow values to new components.
Don't ship a generic dark-mode portfolio with hero sections and glowing stack badges.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text + gradient background).
Don't use Active Window Blue as a decorative accent outside titlebars and focus rings.
Don't add a border-left or border-right stripe larger than 1px as a colored accent.
Don't animate layout properties — transform and opacity only.
Don't use bounce or elastic easing.
Don't add content that reads as AI-assembled with no specific context.
